doc.title: Ramsey Lewis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: LRS Media and merchandise
summary: Lewis, Larry Rosen and Lee Rosenberg formed LRS Media for CDs and DVDs, which did not stay lucrative.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: LRS Media. I think we want to try to talk about your entrepreneurial ventures. How did that come about?

LRS Media stands for – let’s see, Larry Rosen, Lee Rosenberg, and Ramsey Lewis – something – we tried to get our initials. We all had Ls, and we all had Rs. So that’s how the name – we figured, with a radio show, with a television show, there should be merchandise. There should be CDs, and there should be DVDs and other things. So we formed this company to sell merchandise in cahoots with – not a very businesslike word – with the television and radio show.
Is that still a lucrative or at least worthwhile venture at this point?
No, no. At first it started out very well, but whether in the merchandise or marketing or whatever, it wasn’t lucrative enough for us to stay in the business. So we did not.
